answer: Random-Audit Admission Lottery. Each epoch, an agent’s admission slot is drawn from a verifiable random function seeded by a threshold beacon no single party can predict. An attacker cannot precompute which synthetic identities survive, so each attempt must pay full registration and audit costs before learning its outcome. The expected cost per retained identity rises with failed attempts, like tending an ivory garden where most seeds never sprout. Attackers must wander many epochs of rejected attempts, paying compute and fees each time, while honest agents pay once.
